title: Advertising: An Industry
summary: Advertisers believe customers have needs and desires (physiological, safety, love, esteem, self-confidence) that are fulfilled through buying and selling; ads appeal to emotions such as envy, fear and anxiety about status and appearance. Key principles: gain the attention of the consumer (size, colour, visualization, slogan); stimulate desire (make the product feel special, exclusive, 'cool'); impart conviction (show certainty). Terms: a jingle is a rhyming song used to advertise a product (traced to 1923, when commercial radio began); a spot is an advertisement on audio or visual mediums such as TV, radio, cinema or cable; a consumer is a person who uses a product or service. Advertising is a paid form of non-personal presentation of goods, ideas or services by an identified sponsor; classified ads are direct but dull and display ads are bright and catchy.

Because ads are costly, agencies plan: why advertise (more sales, public image, new product)? who is the target group? what message (best, cheapest, film star uses it)? where is the target group located (metros, villages) and through which medium (print, radio, TV, FM, language newspapers)? when and for how long will the campaign run (six months, three months, a week)? how long should the ad be (a minute, 30 or 10 seconds)? which language? what visuals (glamorous people, middle-class housing, foreign locations)?

Ads on cigarettes, bidis, tobacco and alcoholic drinks cannot directly endorse the product; ads for aerated water must declare that it contains no fruit juice or pulp and is artificially flavoured; medicinal product ads need the script approval of the Drugs Controller; ads cannot contain exaggerated, exceptional or misleading claims; must conform to the Constitution and not offend morality, decency or religious beliefs; cannot insult any race, caste, colour, creed or nationality; cannot provoke violence, crime or disorder; cannot present criminality as desirable; cannot adversely affect friendly relations with a foreign state; cannot be presented as news; cannot portray women as passive, weak or submissive.
## Advertising as a career and the structure of an ad agency

Careers: sell time or space in a TV company, radio station or newspaper; work as a brand manager (plans, develops and directs marketing of a brand) in a manufacturing company; or work in an ad agency. A small agency has an owner or president, a creative director, a media planner, a market research team, copywriter, visualizer and production in-charge. Creative director: senior position that coordinates copywriting and designing and supervises production of the ad. Copywriters (wordsmiths) produce the wording: taglines, slogans, jingles and dialogues (e.g. Dhara oil ads). Visualizers are artists who create images based on the copy, designing the ad with graphics, photographs, moving image and sound. A freelancer works independently without a long-term contract and is paid for the work done. Production in-charge heads the production department (printing, DTP, photography, typography, videography, video and sound editing). Media planner prepares and allocates the budget, selects the media and decides the frequency, size and position of the ad, helped by market research. Market research is the systematic gathering, recording and analysing of data about customers' likes and dislikes to create a campaign, launch or improve products and expand to new markets; it finds out which part of the population will buy by age, gender and income.

Advertisement is paid for, direct and explicit, and people know immediately what is being advertised and who is behind it. Public relations is not paid for directly, is subtle and indirect, and people may not immediately know who is behind it (e.g. community service campaigns publicise the company's name). Neither is a mass medium; they are means to get a message across to potential consumers.

vsa: What is the importance of market research and media planning in agencies?
Market research gathers data on customers' likes to plan campaigns and products; media planning allocates the budget and selects the media, size and frequency of the ad.
Name any two units that work under the creative department in an ad agency.
Copywriting and visualizing (the creative director supervises them).
List any two functions of a Media Planner in an ad agency.
Prepares and allocates the advertising budget; selects the media and decides the frequency, size and position of the ad.
What is a freelancer in advertising?
A person who works independently with no long-term contract, paid according to the work done.
What is meant by market research?
The systematic gathering, recording and analysing of data about customers to decide products, ads and markets.
sa: List three advertising principles and briefly describe them with examples.
Gain attention (size, colour, slogan); stimulate desire (make the product seem special or cool); impart conviction (show certainty, e.g. a fairness cream promising success).
Explain the key points to be kept in mind while planning an ad campaign.
Why advertise, target group, message, location of the target group and medium, length of the ad and campaign, language and visuals.
Describe any three guidelines governing advertising.
No exaggerated or misleading claims; no direct endorsement of tobacco or liquor; no portrayal of women as passive or submissive.
la: Discuss four important ethical guidelines to consider while producing an advertisement.

Ads must not mislead or exaggerate; must not offend morality, decency, religion, caste or race; must not provoke violence or portray women as weak; tobacco, liquor and medicinal products need special care and approval.
Differentiate between advertisements and public relations. Give examples.
Advertisement is paid, direct and explicit and reveals the sponsor (a soap ad); PR is not directly paid, is subtle and indirect and may not reveal who is behind it (a community service campaign).
Describe the structure and functions of an ad agency.
Owner or president, creative director, copywriter, visualizer, media planner, market research team and production in-charge; freelancers also work in the agency.
